research_rationale: EO 4109 (December 8, 1924, Calvin Coolidge), read in full in the held ProQuest replica scan (archival_replica_scan_pending_codebook, acceptable_as_original false) and checked against the page image rendered from the held PDF (ProQuest Pre-1937 Orders/PT1-1924-EO-4109.pdf, sha256 e75a8313...; one page; heading 'Executive Order', 'FLORIDA', signature 'CALVIN COOLIDGE', 'The White House, December 8, 1924', '[No. 4109]'; Interior received stamp December 18, 1924; State Department true-copy date December 17, 1924). The OCR layer holds every printed line of the order; its errors ('Executve odber', 'the. same', stamp noise) do not touch the operative words. One operative command: under the act of June 25, 1910 (36 Stat. 847) as amended August 24, 1912 (37 Stat. 497), 'all islands belonging to the United States in Florida situated in the waters off the coast or in the coastal waters of the State' are withdrawn from settlement, location, sale, entry and all forms of appropriation, subject to valid existing rights, 'for classification and in aid of legislation'. No stated effective date; effective on signing. The order states no term and no own-terms end: its purpose (classification and legislation) is not shown to have been completed, and completion would not itself have ended a withdrawal that runs until revoked. First and whole end: EO 8861 (Franklin D. Roosevelt, August 20, 1941), held as an APP mirror transcription (page record checked: MIRROR_DOCUMENTS row heading names EO 8861 and Nos. 4109, 4262 and 4430, date 1941-08-20, text_sha256 equals the held text) and in the held Federal Register text of 6 FR 4289 (August 22, 1941; F.R. Doc. 41-6244, filed August 21, 1941): the three orders 'are hereby revoked, the lands thus released becoming subject to the provisions of Executive Order No. 6964 of February 5, 1935'. EO 8861 states no effective date; recorded as 1941-08-20, the signing date, with publication on August 22, 1941 as the disclosed alternative. Partial later events cited: EO 4372 (January 23, 1926; ProQuest scan, page image checked) revoked EO 4109 as to the abandoned military reservations on Batton Islands and Key Biscayne; EO 4485 (July 24, 1926; ProQuest scan, page image checked) as to fractional sec. 6, T. 1 N., R. 29 E., on Amelia Island; EO 8725 (March 29, 1941; aerial gunnery ranges; held Federal Register text) 'shall take precedence over but shall not rescind or revoke' EO 4109 for its lands, recorded as a later event that ended nothing. Two further partial events are held but disclosed rather than cited, because the dossier offers them only as APP transcriptions while official Federal Register copies are held (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_7993.txt and EO_8508.txt) and the working-text gate refuses a transcription when an official copy exists: EO 7993 (October 27, 1938; Great White Heron Refuge) superseded EO 4109 'insofar as such withdrawals affect the above-described lands', and EO 8508 (August 8, 1940; antiaircraft firing range, 195.26 acres in T. 3 S., R. 31 W.) superseded it 'as to any of the above-described lands'. Each released only named lands before the whole revocation, so neither changes the first end or the status. The 1989 OFR codification disposition table (held: jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/DISPOSITION_1989.csv) lists EO 4109 as 'Amended by EOs 4372, 4485, 7993, 8508' and 'Revoked by EO 8861', which matches this inventory of events. Contrary evidence checked: the dossier's actor records for EOs 8858, 8859 and 8860 come from the same Federal Register pages (6 FR 4288-4289) as EO 8861 and are page-neighbour artefacts; the held FR texts of EOs 7994, 8509, 8510 and 8724 that mention EO 4109 are the same pages as EOs 7993, 8508 and 8725; a citation search of every held order text found no instrument after August 20, 1941 that names EO 4109.
savings_reason: EO 8861 contains no savings clause. The lands it released became 'subject to the provisions of Executive Order No. 6964 of February 5, 1935'; that continuing withdrawal is EO 6964's own command and belongs to its lifecycle, not a residual of EO 4109. Valid existing rights were excepted from the withdrawal from the start and were never affected by it. Lands reserved by EOs 7993 and 8508 continued under those orders, not under EO 4109.
earlier_end_check: No earlier whole end. The four earlier events (EOs 4372, 4485, 7993, 8508) each name the lands they release or reserve, and the withdrawal continued for all other Florida islands. EO 6964 (February 5, 1935), the general withdrawal of public lands in the eastern states, overlapped EO 4109 without revoking it (EOs 7993, 8508 and 8861 all treat EO 4109 as still operating afterwards). No statute naming EO 4109 is held or found.
scope_check: Whole order is one clause, one withdrawal of one class of land (Florida islands). Partial events are recorded as later events; the whole clause ended with EO 8861.
independent_command_check: No independent command. The citation of the 1910 act and its 1912 amendment is authority; 'subject to any valid existing rights' is an exception to the withdrawal, not a separate command.

research_rationale: EO 4262 (July 3, 1925, Calvin Coolidge), Alabama, Florida and Mississippi. Page image of the held ProQuest PDF (PT1-1925-EO-4262.pdf, sha256 e9afa11a...) checked: two operative commands, (1) a townsite withdrawal under R.S. 2380 of Lot D, sec. 24, T. 9 S., R. 3 E., St. Stephens Meridian, Alabama (49 acres) and Lot 1, sec. 33, T. 3 S., R. 32 W., Tallahassee Meridian, Florida (40.10 acres), 'to be disposed of under Sec. 2381', and (2) a withdrawal under the 1910 act of all mainland within three miles of the coast in the three states and all islands off Alabama and Mississippi, pending classification and legislation. Whole end is established from held sources: EO 8861 (August 20, 1941, held APP mirror and 6 FR 4289) revokes 'No. 4262 of July 3, 1925'. Held partial events: EO 4321 (October 13, 1925, lands within national forests), EO 4489 (August 3, 1926), EO 4574 (January 28, 1927), EO 5011-B (December 3, 1928) (all ProQuest scans, page images checked, excerpts in this packet's supplement), EO 5191 (September 13, 1929, APP live harvest only), EO 8725 (March 29, 1941, precedence without revocation). Blocked because the held OCR text of the original drops a printed line ('under Sec. 2380 U. S. Revised Statutes, subject to valid existing rights in and to'), so the complete-text confirmation and an exact quotation of the townsite clause are impossible, and the single machine clause must be split into the two commands. For the townsite clause, whether either lot was sold under R.S. 2381 before 1941 (which would end that reservation for the lot earlier) is not established.

research_rationale: EO 4430 (April 23, 1926, Calvin Coolidge), read in full in the held ProQuest replica scan (archival_replica_scan_pending_codebook, acceptable_as_original false) and checked against the page image rendered from the held PDF (ProQuest Pre-1937 Orders/PT1-1926-EO-4430.pdf, sha256 f52572ba...; one page; 'Executive Order', 'Michigan and Wisconsin', 'CALVIN COOLIDGE', 'The White House, April 23, 1926', '[No. 4430]'; Interior received stamp May 3, 1926; State Department true copy May 1, 1926; a handwritten note '8861 - 8/20/41 ... Fed Reg 8/22/41'). The OCR layer holds every printed line; it misreads the date as 'April 28' (the image reads April 23, as do EO 8861, EO 4446 and EO 7814) and garbles words such as 'Pursudhit' and 'rigIts' without changing the operative content. One operative command: under the act of June 25, 1910 as amended August 24, 1912, and with the exception of lands whose disposal is authorized by the act of July 5, 1884, all public lands 'bordering on meandered lakes and all islands therein in the States of Michigan and Wisconsin, and all lands within three miles of the shore of Lakes Michigan, Huron or Superior, in said States, and all islands within the lakes last mentioned' are withdrawn from settlement, location, sale, entry and all forms of appropriation, subject to valid existing rights, pending classification and legislation. No stated effective date; effective on signing; no stated term. First and whole end: EO 8861 (August 20, 1941), held as an APP mirror transcription (page record checked: heading names EO 8861 and No. 4430, date 1941-08-20, text_sha256 equals the held text) and in the held Federal Register text of 6 FR 4289 (August 22, 1941): 'Executive Orders No. 4109 of December 8, 1924, No. 4262 of July 3, 1925, and No. 4430 of April 23, 1926 ... are hereby revoked, the lands thus released becoming subject to the provisions of Executive Order No. 6964'. Recorded as 1941-08-20 (signing); publication on August 22, 1941 is the disclosed alternative. Partial later event cited: EO 4446 (May 21, 1926; ProQuest scan, page image checked), revoking EO 4430 as to Wisconsin lands whose disposal the act of February 27, 1925 authorizes. Further partial events are disclosed but not cited; each ended the withdrawal only for named lands before the whole revocation, so none changes the first end or the status: EO 7795 (January 21, 1938; Huron Migratory Bird Refuge), whose reservation 'supersedes as to any of the above-described islands affected thereby the temporary withdrawal ... made by Executive Order No. 4430', and EO 7814 (February 15, 1938; lot 1, sec. 9, T. 32 N., R. 9 W., Fourth Principal Meridian, Wisconsin), both held as APP transcriptions (page records checked) and as official Federal Register texts (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_7795.txt, EO_7814.txt) that the dossier does not offer as citable alternatives (its Federal Register record for EO 7795 is sliced from the contents page, not the order), so the working-text gate refuses the transcriptions; EO 5366 (June 13, 1930, 160 acres in T. 27 N., R. 15 W., Michigan, for a homestead application) and EO 5386 (June 30, 1930, lands selected by Michigan under the act of July 31, 1912) are held as APP transcriptions but their supplement excerpts came out ungraded because the fragment registry holds two registrations of the same text (live and mirror), so the assembler cannot cite them; a partial revocation of EO 4430 'in so far as it affects any of the above-described lands' (with revocation of the lighthouse withdrawals of July 21 and October 20, 1874) is printed at 3 FR 2800 (Federal Register of November 30, 1938) beside Proclamation 2313 of November 25, 1938 in the held text jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_8014.txt, but its acting instrument cannot be fixed from the column-mixed OCR without the page image; Proclamation 2318, listed in the 1989 OFR codification disposition table (held: jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/DISPOSITION_1989.csv) as amending EO 4430, is not held. That table lists EO 4430 as 'Amended by Procs. 2313, 2318; EOs 4446, 5366, 5386, 7795, 7814' and 'Revoked by EO 8861'. Contrary evidence checked: the dossier records for EO 7794 and the dossier's missing-provision pointers to EOs 7796, 7815 and 8014 are Federal Register page-neighbour artefacts (EO 7796 concerns state offices, EO 7815 West Point positions, EO 8014 Alaska military reservations); EOs 8858-8860 likewise share 6 FR 4288-4289 with EO 8861. A citation search of every held order text found no instrument after August 20, 1941 naming EO 4430.

research_rationale: EO 5038 (February 2, 1929, Calvin Coolidge) temporarily withdrew described lands in California for classification pending determination whether to add them to the Pinnacles National Monument; it continues 'unless and until revoked by the President or by act of Congress'. Original held as an APP mirror transcription. No later instrument is in the dossier. The held 1989 OFR codification disposition table and the held NARA disposition page (jobs/hathi-gpo-orders/output/discovery/nara_executive-orders-02.html) record 'Amended by Proc. 2528' and 'Revoked by PLO 1397'. Neither instrument's text is held, so neither the end date nor whether Proc. 2528 already absorbed the lands into the monument (an earlier partial or whole supersession) can be established.

research_rationale: EO 5214 (October 30, 1929, Herbert Hoover) withdrew four areas of land and water in Alaska (Cold Bay-Dolgoi Island, Port Graham and others) for Navy Department naval purposes 'until this order is revoked by the President or Congress'. Original held as an APP mirror. Held partial event: EO 8736 (April 14, 1941; 6 FR 1984 and APP) revoked it as to a tract of the Cold Bay-Dolgoi Island Naval Reservation. The BLM PLO table (web, not held) lists PLO 903 (July 3, 1953, 18 FR 4048) 'revoking in part EO No. 5214' for Air-Navigation Site Withdrawal No. 261, and PLO 945 (March 18, 1954, 19 FR 1583) 'revoking EO No. 5214 of Oct. 30, 1929', amended by PLO 956 (19 FR 2353). None of these PLO texts is held, so the whole end cannot be quoted. The held 1989 disposition table has no row for EO 5214, although PLO 945 falls in its period; this is a coverage gap of that table, not evidence that the order survived.

research_rationale: EO 6143 (May 23, 1933, Franklin D. Roosevelt) temporarily withdrew public lands in New Mexico to aid the State in making exchange selections under the act of June 15, 1926; it continues until revoked. Original held as an APP mirror. Held partial events: EO 6362 (partial revocation) and EO 7442 (modification for War Department use). The BLM PLO tables (web, not held) list partial revocations PLO 5102 (August 10, 1971, 36 FR 14695), PLO 5127 (September 25, 1971, 36 FR 19027), PLO 5374 (July 30, 1973, 38 FR 21168) and PLO 5679 (August 20, 1979, 44 FR 50344), and the whole revocation PLO 6459 (August 16, 1983, 48 FR 40724; corrected by PLO 6589, 50 FR 9428), which the held 1989 disposition table and NARA page also give as 'Revoked by PLO 6459'. FLPMA section 701 (1976) saved the withdrawal until then and is a continuity point. Blocked because the PLO 6459 text is not held.

research_rationale: EO 6604 (February 16, 1934, Franklin D. Roosevelt) temporarily withdrew all public lands in named townships of Nebraska and South Dakota for soil classification; no stated term. Original held as an APP mirror. No later instrument is in the dossier and the held 1989 table has no row for it. The BLM PLO table (web, not held) lists PLO 711 (April 10, 1951, 16 FR 3348): 'Nebraska and South Dakota; revoking EO No. 6604 of Feb. 16, 1934; withdrawing public lands for soil classification.' research_rationale: Hub case, examined for about 25 minutes. EO 6910 (November 26, 1934) temporarily withdrew 'all of the vacant, unreserved and unappropriated public land' in twelve western states for classification pending the Taylor Grazing Act and for conservation, 'subject to existing rights', until revoked. Provisional status YES. The dossier holds 53 distinct later-actor records (180 with alternatives) and the later-events data 210+ events; every one examined names particular lands (amendments excluding tracts, supersessions by refuges, ranges and military withdrawals, partial revocations, or 'take precedence over but shall not rescind or revoke'), and none is a whole revocation. The held 1989 disposition table classes EO 6910 as 'Public lands' (not ended) with 80+ amending instruments, and the visible portions of the BLM PLO tables show no PLO revoking EO 6910 in whole. Current-law leads (machine, not held as text): 43 CFR 2520.0-8(c) ('Unsurveyed public land withdrawn by Executive Orders 6910 and 6964 ... is not subject to appropriation, under the desert-land laws, until ...'), 43 CFR 2400.0-3 and 2300.0-3(b) (background statements), and 16 U.S.C. 460y-6 (King Range, 1970: lands 'withdrawn by Executive Order Numbered 6910'). These support a continuing withdrawal for unclassified lands, with FLPMA section 701 (1976) as a continuity point, but no held legal text slice exists for any of them and the current predicate through 2026-10-14 needs either a held current regulation that operates on the withdrawal or BLM land-status records showing an active EO 6910 withdrawal. A claim also needs a decision on whether the 210 partial events must each be listed (they do not change a YES).

research_rationale: EO 7373 (May 20, 1936, Franklin D. Roosevelt) established the Desert Game Range, Nevada. The dossier's original is the Federal Register of May 22, 1936 (opus-media-match text, grade held_text_lead), which is not a registered working-text grade, so assembly would fail; an APP transcription (executive-order-7373-establishing-the-desert-game-range-nevada) exists but the dossier did not select it. Of the dossier's 86 later-actor records only EOs 8578 (1940), 9019 and 9020 (1942) name EO 7373, all 'take precedence over, but shall not rescind or revoke'; the rest are EO 6910/6964 events mis-attached through the 'Amended EO 6910' link. The held 1989 table and NARA page record 'Revoked by PLO 4079'; the BLM PLO table (web) lists PLO 570 (March 2, 1949, 14 FR 1086) 'revoking in part EO No. 7373'. The area continues as the Desert National Wildlife Refuge under later instruments, which is continuity of the area, not of this order.

Roosevelt) established the Winnemucca Migratory Bird Refuge, Nevada (identity from the held APP text executive-order-7435-establishing-winnemucca-migratory-bird-refuge-nevada.txt). Revoked, per the BLM PLO table (web, not held), by PLO 936 (February 4, 1954, 19 FR 769). Blocked because PLO 936 is not held.

research_rationale: EO 7509 (December 11, 1936, Franklin D. Roosevelt) established the Fort Peck Game Range, Montana; provisional status YES. The dossier's original is a wrong document (the Water Resources Development Act of 2000, Pub. L. 106-541), which produced 1,987 machine clauses; an APP transcription of EO 7509 is held but was not selected. Status evidence conflicts: the held 1989 table and NARA page say 'Revoked by PLO 4588'; Wikipedia (web) describes PLO 4588 (March 25, 1969) as establishing the UL Bend National Wildlife Refuge, which suggests a partial revocation; the BLM PLO table (web) lists PLO 5498 (April 25, 1975, 40 FR 18996, transfer of jurisdiction of the Charles M. Russell National Wildlife Range), PLO 5500 (40 FR 23472, correction) and PLO 5635 (April 25, 1978, 43 FR 19046) 'amending EO No. 7509 ... change of name to Charles M. Russell' National Wildlife Refuge. An instrument amending EO 7509 in 1978 implies it was still operative after PLO 4588, which supports the YES; Pub. L. 94-223 (1976) placed game ranges under Fish and Wildlife Service administration. None of these texts is held.

Roosevelt) established the Lenore Lake Migratory Bird Refuge, Washington, superseding EOs 5818 and 6964 for its lands (identity from the held APP text). The dossier's original is a wrong document (the Federal Register of November 14, 1936, Treasury income-tax Regulations 94), which produced 99 machine clauses. The BLM PLO table (web) lists PLO 658 (August 15, 1950, 15 FR 5535: 'revoking in part EO No. 7510 ... establishing the Lenore Lake Migratory Bird Refuge') and PLO 1249 (November 7, 1955, 20 FR 8471: 'reserving lands as Lenore Game Range; revoking EO No. 7510 of Dec. 11, 1936'); the held 1989 table also records 'Revoked by PLO 1249'. Neither PLO text is held.
